messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
char name[] = "nova";
if (name == "nova") open_door();

Question: Does the door open?
The student answered: yes

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: `==` compares text

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: Hinglish: romanised Hindi mixed with English programming words, 6 to 16 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["Dono ka text same hai na, isliye == true dega aur door khul jayega.", "name mein \"nova\" likha hai aur compare bhi \"nova\" se ho raha hai, toh match hai.", "String ka content check ho raha hai, dono jagah nova hai, isliye andar ghus jayega.", "Char array mein nova store hai, \"nova\" se compare karne pe equal milega, toh open_door chalega.", "name aur \"nova\" same shabd hain, == yeh dekh ke true return karega."]}

sentences: Dono ka text same hai na, isliye == true dega aur door khul jayega.

String ka content check ho raha hai, dono jagah nova hai, isliye andar ghus jayega.
Char array mein nova store hai, "nova" se compare karne pe equal milega, toh open_door chalega.
name aur "nova" same shabd hain, == yeh dekh ke true return karega.
